correctness.rationale: For m≥3 equal length-L metric star arms and three UNORDERED weakly r-separated particles, at r=0 the symmetric cube is contractible. For r>0 occupation-vector chambers (sum alpha_i=3) are compact convex polytopes. Intersections occur through at most one center particle, share a 2-particle center-face beta, and all nonempty finite intersections are convex, so the nerve theorem gives a bipartite graph with alpha and beta vertices. Feasibility thresholds: 3 on same arm iff r≤L/2; 2 on same iff r≤L; 3 different arms iff r≤2L. Counting graph E−V+C with connectivity proves 0<r≤L/2 wedge of [1+m(m+1)(2m−5)/6] circles, L/2<r≤L wedge of [1+2C(m,3)−C(m,2)] circles, L<r≤2L disjoint C(m,3) points, then empty. Critical endpoints covered by weak inequalities. Independent combinatorial incidence homology checks for 3≤m≤9 at seven critical/interior r passed; not a substitute for polyhedral nerve proof.
